cues.en: and so what I would do is I would count trying to count up to a minute actually it took me say I count to 48 and it would be one minute so I calibrate myself and I would count minute and 48, I think I was counting seconds but it's close enough And then it turns out if you repeat that, you can do very accurately. When you get to 48 or 47 or 49, not far off, you're very close to a minute.
cues.zh: 所以我当时会怎么做呢，我会去数数，试着数到一分钟，实际上我大概数到 48 的时候就是一分钟，所以我校准了自己，我会数一分钟零 48 秒——我想我当时数的是秒，但也八九不离十了。然后你会发现如果你重复这个过程，你可以数得很准。当你数到 48、47 或 49 时，差得不远，非常接近一分钟。

cues.en: And I would try to find out what affected that time sense, and whether I could do anything at the same time as I was counting
cues.zh: 然后我试图找出是什么影响了这种时间感，以及在我数数的同时我能不能做点别的

cues.zh: 我还得列个清单。有多少双袜子？我记得大概是六双还是八双袜子，而我没法数它们，因为数数的“机器”正在被占用，直到我发现可以把它们排成某种图案来识别数量。

cues.en: And so I learned a way after practicing by which I could go down the lines of type in newspapers and see them in groups three three three one, that's a group of 10, three three three one without saying the numbers, just seeing the grouping.
cues.zh: 于是练习之后，我学会了一种方法：我能沿着报纸的排版行往下看，把它们按三、三、三、一分组，也就是一组 10 行，三三三一，不用念出数字，只看到分组。

cues.en: I could therefore count the lines of type I practiced
cues.zh: 因此我能数出我练习过的排版行数

cues.en: in the newspaper at the same time I was counting internally the seconds and so I would come I could do this fantastic trick of saying 48 that's a one minute and there are 67 lines of type. See?
cues.zh: 在报纸上，同时心里数秒，于是我能做到这个绝活：说 48，也就是一分钟，这里有 67 行排版。明白吗？

cues.zh: 而且能知道大概内容，但我不能说话。我什么也说不了，因为当然，我有点……数数时我其实在心里对自己说话。我会在脑子里说一、二、三。

cues.zh: John Tookie 当时也是普林斯顿的数学家，我们讨论过很多次，我跟他说了这些实验和我的能力，他说这太荒唐了，他说。

cues.en: He says I don't see why you would have any difficulty talking whatsoever,

cues.en: So I couldn't believe on this, but we calibrated him. It was fifty two for him to get to sixty seconds or whatever. I don't remember the numbers now.
cues.zh: 所以我不信这个，但我们校准了他。他数到五十二就以为到六十秒了，或者随便多少。我现在不记得数字了。

cues.en: And then he'd say, alright, he said, what do you want me to say? Mary had a little lamb, I can speak about anything, blah blah blah blah blah blah, 52, it's a minute, he was right,
cues.zh: 然后他说，好吧，他说，你想让我说什么？玛丽有只小羊羔，我什么都能讲，巴拉巴拉巴拉巴拉，52，一分钟，他说得对，

cues.en: and I couldn't possibly do that, and he wanted me to read because he couldn't believe it, and then we compared notes and it turned out that when he thought of counting, what he did inside his head when he counted was he saw a tape with numbers that when clink clink clink the tape would change with the numbers printed on it he could see.
cues.zh: 而我不可能做到，他想让我读，因为他不敢相信，然后我们核对了一下，结果发现，当他想着数数时，他数数时脑子里做的是，他看到一条带数字的纸带，咔嗒咔嗒咔嗒，纸带上印着的数字会变化，他能看见。

cues.en: Well, since it's sort of an optical system that he's using and not voice, he could speak as much as he wanted, but if he had to read, then he couldn't look at his clock.
cues.zh: 嗯，因为他用的算是一种视觉系统，而不是声音，所以他想说多少都行，但如果他要读，就没法看他的钟。

cues.en: Whereas for me, was the other way, and that's where I discovered,
cues.zh: 而对我来说，情况正好相反，这就是我发现，

cues.en: at least in this very simple operation of counting,
cues.zh: 至少在这个非常简单的数数操作中，

cues.en: the great difference in what goes on in the head
cues.zh: 头脑中发生的事情存在巨大差异

cues.en: when people think they're doing the same thing.
cues.zh: 当人们以为自己是在做同一件事时。

cues.zh: 可能真的会——如果我们能把它放进彼此的脑子里——完全不同。
